This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER
This is the fifth application filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on behalf of the applicant for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. The applicant is apprehending his arrest in FIR No.320/2018 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station Civil Line Satna, District Satna, for the offence under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is seeking interim protection mainly on the ground that in the statement of the witness recorded during the pendency of a civil suit pending between the parties, it has come that the present applicant has not committed any fraud.

He submits Dilip Agrawal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61364997/
1 that there is a civil dispute between the parties as a transaction took place between them in respect of some civil transaction.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that one of the co-accused persons has been granted bail by this Court under Section 439 of CrPC and the present applicant can be granted interim protection.

He submits that the applicant is ready to provide full assistance to the prosecution during the course of investigation.
4.

On the other hand, the counsel for the State has opposed the submission made by the counsel for the applicant and submitted that the application for grant of anticipatory bail has already been rejected by the Court on merit not only once, but also on several occasions, therefore, the application under the same head cannot be considered again only because some statement of the witness have come in a pending civil suit.

5. Considering the submissions made by the counsel for the parties and after perusal of record, I am also of the opinion that the bail application under Section 438 of CrPC cannot be considered only because one of the co-accused persons has been granted bail under Section 439 of CrPC.

Therefore,
the same is rejected.

6. However, the applicant is free to move regular bail application before the trial Court and try to convince the Court about the fact that one of the co- accused persons has been granted regular bail and also on the basis of statement of witnesses recorded in a pending civil suit.
It is made clear that if application under Section 439 of CrPC is moved before the trial Court, the same be considered possibly on the same day.
7. With the aforesaid, this bail application is dismissed.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE ac/-
